text:
jess: heads-up — after enabling time-slice and MIG mixed nodepools in eu-west1 we started seeing autoscaler churn. Pods stay Pending with `InsufficientGPU` even though nodes show free MIG slices. anyone seen this interplay before? :thinking:

omar: can you paste the cluster-autoscaler logs around the scale-up events and the node description (allocatable resources)? curious if CA is treating MIG/time-slice resources as unknown. also which device-plugin version?

jess: here's the log bit (trimmed):
```
I0410 09:02:58.123456 1 scale_up.go:412] No candidates for scale up: insufficient resources: nvidia.com/gpu: requested 2, available 0
I0410 09:03:01.654321 1 scale_up.go:478] Scale up triggered for nodegroup gpu-timeslice-eu-west1-a: +2
```
node allocatable shows `nvidia.com/gpu` = 0 but `nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb` = 8 on some nodes. device-plugin = 0.11.

tia: that explains it — CA only understands regular `nvidia.com/gpu` by default. when we surface MIG slices as separate resources the plugin needs to register them under the well-known resource names CA expects, or we must teach CA about the alternate resource name. we did something similar in us-west where the plugin maps `nvidia.com/mig-*` -> `nvidia.com/gpu` via a CRD shim. do we have that shim enabled here?

marta: also fyi when we enable time-slicing (vGPU/time-share) nodes advertise a custom resource like `nvidia.com/gpu.timeslice/4` in our setup. cluster-autoscaler doesn't have logic for custom slash-names either, so it will believe there are zero GPUs for pods requesting `nvidia.com/gpu`. two approaches: (1) make the device-plugin advertise the canonical `nvidia.com/gpu` (with fractional values surfaced as integer counts using a packing layer), or (2) run a custom CA fork that recognizes our naming. option (1) is safer operationally.

omar: short-term patch we used before: change pod requests to the actual advertised resource name e.g. `resources.requests: \n  nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb: 1` but that requires all schedulers and helm charts to change — brittle. better to make the plugin export stable names.

jess: is there a kubelet/device-plugin config snippet we can apply quickly?

tia: yes — for the MIG plugin we used a simple mapping configmap on the plugin daemonset:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: mig-plugin-config
data:
  advertise_as: |
    - from: "nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb"
      to:   "nvidia.com/gpu"
    - from: "nvidia.com/mig-2g.10gb"
      to:   "nvidia.com/gpu"
```
That lets CA see `nvidia.com/gpu` counts. caveat: you must be careful with fractional semantics — we round down and rely on packing admission to avoid overcommit.

marta: another operational wrinkle — time-sliced nodes hit network bursting limits in eu-west1 because our pod egress crosses a NAT gateway. That delays node readiness (kubelet cni handshake), which makes CA think new nodes are unhealthy and triggers more scale-ups. Check cloud NAT / route quotas. We saw 20-30s extra readiness latency per node.

omar: suggested CA flags that helped reduce churn in prod: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45 --max-node-provision-time=20m --balance-similar-node-groups=false`. increasing `--max-node-provision-time` is important when startup probes or custom CNI slow boot.

infra-bot: [alert] autoscaler: scaled up 3 nodes (gpu-timeslice-eu-west1-a) at 2026-04-10T09:03:01Z — reason: pending pods exceed capacity.

jess: good note about NAT. we'll run a quick check on cloud NAT logs and increase max-provision-time. also will try the plugin mapping config in a canary pool.

tia: short-term scheduling tip: add a topology/anti-affinity so pods prefer different nodes for time-slice pools. packs can lead to noisy neighbours on shared hardware. example: `podAntiAffinity` with `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` on `kubernetes.io/hostname`. helps stabilization until we fix the resource naming.

marta: cost note — our numbers from last month: fractional/time-slice increased GPU utilization from ~48%->~72% (good), but increased per-pod tail-latency 95th by ~12% and bumped cross-zone egress by ~10% due to more preemptible placement churn in eu-west. net savings on GPU bill ~30% but we need to watch SLO regressions.

jess: thanks all. action items: (1) canary the plugin mapping in a small nodepool today, (2) bump CA's `--max-node-provision-time`, (3) check cloud NAT logs and quota, (4) add podAntiAffinity to critical workloads. i'll update once canary is live. :thumbsup:
